# Google Style Template - Design Specification

> Suitable for tech company annual reports, work summaries, technical sharing, data presentations, and similar scenarios.

---

## I. Template Overview

| Property       | Description                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Template Name** | google_style (Google Style Template)                    |
| **Use Cases**  | Annual work reports, technical sharing, project showcases, data-driven presentations |
| **Design Tone** | Professional, modern, clean and restrained, data-driven, generous whitespace |
| **Theme Mode** | Light theme (white/light gray background + Google brand color accents) |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property       | Value                         |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **Format**     | Standard 16:9                 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px                |
| **viewBox**    | `0 0 1280 720`                |
| **Page Margins** | Left/Right 60px, Top 50px, Bottom 50px |
| **Safe Area**  | x: 60-1220, y: 50-670        |

---

## III. Color Scheme

### Google Brand Colors

| Role             | Value       | Notes                                |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Google Blue**  | `#4285F4`   | Primary titles, key data, main buttons |
| **Google Red**   | `#EA4335`   | Important emphasis, warning info     |
| **Google Yellow**| `#FBBC04`   | Auxiliary icons, secondary emphasis   |
| **Google Green** | `#34A853`   | Success indicators, positive data    |

### Professional Colors

| Role           | Value       | Usage                                |
| -------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Deep Blue**  | `#1A237E`   | Titles, core text, dark emphasis     |
| **Deep Blue Gradient Start** | `#1A73E8` | Gradient title start point  |
| **Deep Blue Gradient End** | `#0D47A1` | Gradient title end point      |
| **Main Background White** | `#FFFFFF` | Page main background           |
| **Light Gray Background** | `#F8F9FA` | Card inner background, auxiliary areas |
| **Light Gray Border** | `#E8EAED` | Dividers, borders, grid lines     |

### Text Colors

| Role           | Value       | Usage                                |
| -------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Primary Text** | `#1A237E` | Titles, important text               |
| **Body Text**  | `#5F6368`   | Body content, descriptions           |
| **Secondary Text** | `#9AA0A6` | Annotations, page numbers, tips    |
| **White Text** | `#FFFFFF`   | Text on dark backgrounds             |

### Chart Colors (use in order)

| Order | Value       | Notes          |
| ----- | ----------- | -------------- |
| 1     | `#4285F4`   | Google Blue    |
| 2     | `#34A853`   | Google Green   |
| 3     | `#FBBC04`   | Google Yellow  |
| 4     | `#EA4335`   | Google Red     |

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Stack

**Font Stack**: `system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`

> Uses system UI font stack to ensure cross-platform consistency and optimal rendering.

### Font Size Hierarchy

| Level  | Usage                | Size   | Weight      |
| ------ | -------------------- | ------ | ----------- |
| H1     | Cover main title     | 52px   | 700 (Bold)  |
| H2     | Page main title      | 46px   | 700 (Bold)  |
| H3     | Module/section title | 28px   | 600         |
| H4     | Card title/subtitle  | 24px   | 600         |
| P      | Body content         | 20px   | 400         |
| Data   | Large data numbers   | 56px   | 700 (Bold)  |
| Label  | Data labels/descriptions | 16px | 500        |
| Sub    | Auxiliary text/page number | 14px | 400       |

---

## V. Page Structure

### General Layout

| Area               | Position/Height | Description                            |
| ------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **Top Decorative Bar** | y=0, h=6px  | Four-color gradient bar, spanning full width |
| **Title Area**     | y=50, h=60px    | Page title + title underline           |
| **Content Area**   | y=130, h=500px  | Main content area                      |
| **Footer**         | y=660, h=60px   | Four-color dot decoration + optional page number |

### Signature Design Elements

#### 1. Four-Color Gradient Top Bar
```
linearGradient: #4285F4 → #EA4335 → #FBBC04 → #34A853
height: 6px, width: 100%
```

#### 2. Title Underline (Four-Color Segments)
```
Blue: 150px → Red: 70px → Yellow: 70px → Green: 170px
stroke-width: 4px, y: 20px below title
```

#### 3. KPI Data Card
```
Size: 280×140px
Border radius: 16px
Border: 3px, using corresponding brand color
Shadow: Subtle shadow for depth
```

#### 4. Four-Color Dot Decoration
```
Used in footer or as dividers
radius: 6-14px (varies)
spacing: 30-50px
```

#### 5. Left Four-Color Vertical Bar
```
Cover page exclusive
width: 10px, 4 segments, 180px each
Color order: Blue → Red → Yellow → Green
```

---

## VI. Page Types

### 1. Cover Page (01_cover.svg)

- Light gradient background (white to light blue/light green)
- Left four-color vertical bar decoration
- Centered rounded white content card (with subtle shadow)
- Gradient main title + subtitle
- Four-color segmented divider line
- Speaker info (name, title, date)
- Bottom four-color dot decoration

### 2. Table of Contents Page (02_toc.svg)

- White background + top four-color gradient bar
- Page title + blue underline
- Chapter list (left brand-color dots + numbers + titles)
- Optional: right-side decorative graphics or data stats

### 3. Chapter Page (02_chapter.svg)

- Dark gradient background (deep blue to darker blue)
- Large chapter number (gradient or white)
- Chapter title (white, large font)
- English subtitle (white, semi-transparent)
- Four-color decorative elements

### 4. Content Page (03_content.svg)

- White background
- Top four-color gradient bar
- Page title + blue underline
- Flexible content area (supports multiple layouts)
- Bottom four-color dot decoration

### 5. Ending Page (04_ending.svg)

- Light gradient background
- Centered rounded white content card
- Gradient "Thank You!" title
- Four-color divider line
- Acknowledgment list (brand-color dots + names/items)
- Closing remarks + bottom four-color dots

---

## VII. Layout Patterns

| Pattern                | Use Cases                          |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| **Centered Card**      | Cover, ending, key points          |
| **Left Text Right Image** | Text description + chart/KPI area |
| **KPI Grid (2×2/2×3)** | Data overview, key metrics display |
| **Three-Column Cards** | Project lists, feature introductions |
| **Four Quadrants**     | Category display, SWOT analysis    |
| **Top-Bottom Split**   | Two related topics side by side    |
| **Timeline**           | Development history, roadmap       |
| **Dashboard Style**    | Multi-metric data dashboard        |

---

## VIII. Spacing Guidelines

| Element              | Value    |
| -------------------- | -------- |
| Page margins         | 60px     |
| Title-to-content gap | 30-40px  |
| Module gap           | 60-80px  |
| Card gap             | 20-24px  |
| Card padding         | 20px     |
| Card border radius   | 16px     |
| Icon-to-text gap     | 15px     |

---

## IX. SVG Technical Constraints

### Mandatory Rules

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Use `<rect>` elements for backgrounds
3. Use `<tspan>` for text wrapping (no `<foreignObject>`)
4. Use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` for transparency
5. Define gradients using `<linearGradient>` within `<defs>`

### Prohibited Elements

The following SVG features are prohibited (not PPT-compatible):

- `clipPath`, `mask`
- `<style>` tag, `class` attribute
- `foreignObject`
- `textPath`
- `animate*` animation elements
- `script`
- `marker`, `marker-end`
- `rgba()` color format (use HEX + opacity instead)

### Shadow Implementation

Since `filter` may affect PPT compatibility:
- Use subtle border color variations to simulate shadows
- Or accept that `filter` may be ignored in older PPT versions, though it works well in newer versions

---

## X. Placeholder Specification

Templates use `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` format placeholders:

| Placeholder            | Description              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `{{TITLE}}`            | Main title               |
| `{{SUBTITLE}}`         | Subtitle/department info |
| `{{SPEAKER_NAME}}`     | Speaker name             |
| `{{SPEAKER_TITLE}}`    | Speaker title/position   |
| `{{DATE}}`             | Date                     |
| `{{PAGE_TITLE}}`       | Page title               |
| `{{CHAPTER_NUM}}`      | Chapter number           |
| `{{CHAPTER_TITLE}}`    | Chapter title            |
| `{{CHAPTER_TITLE_EN}}` | Chapter English subtitle |
| `{{PAGE_NUM}}`         | Page number              |
| `{{CONTENT_AREA}}`     | Content area placeholder |

---

## XI. Color Application Examples

### KPI Card Color Rules

| Card Order | Border Color | Number Color | Applicable Content |
| ---------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------------------ |
| 1st        | `#4285F4`    | `#4285F4`    | Core projects/main metrics |
| 2nd        | `#34A853`    | `#34A853`    | Cost/efficiency metrics |
| 3rd        | `#EA4335`    | `#EA4335`    | Reliability/risk   |
| 4th        | `#FBBC04`    | `#FBBC04`    | Performance/growth |

### List Item Colors

- Use the four brand colors in rotation for list bullet colors
- Keep text in a consistent deep blue `#1A237E`

---

## XII. Usage Instructions

1. Copy the template to the project directory `templates/`
2. Select the appropriate page type based on content needs
3. Use placeholders to mark content that needs replacement
4. Strictly follow the Google brand four-color scheme
5. Maintain generous whitespace to highlight key information
6. Data-driven: use large numbers + small labels to display KPIs

---

_This specification is based on Google Material Design principles, adapted for PPT Master project requirements_

164	
165	- Dark gradient background (deep blue to darker blue)
166	- Large chapter number (gradient or white)
167	- Chapter title (white, large font)
168	- English subtitle (white, semi-transparent)
169	- Four-color decorative elements
170	
171	### 4. Content Page (03_content.svg)
172	
173	- White background
174	- Top four-color gradient bar
175	- Page title + blue underline
176	- Flexible content area (supports multiple layouts)
177	- Bottom four-color dot decoration
178	
179	### 5. Ending Page (04_ending.svg)
180	
181	- Light gradient background
182	- Centered rounded white content card
183	- Gradient "Thank You!" title
184	- Four-color divider line
185	- Acknowledgment list (brand-color dots + names/items)
186	- Closing remarks + bottom four-color dots
187	
188	---
189	
190	## VII. Layout Patterns
191	
192	| Pattern                | Use Cases                          |
193	| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
194	| **Centered Card**      | Cover, ending, key points          |
195	| **Left Text Right Image** | Text description + chart/KPI area |
196	| **KPI Grid (2×2/2×3)** | Data overview, key metrics display |
197	| **Three-Column Cards** | Project lists, feature introductions |
198	| **Four Quadrants**     | Category display, SWOT analysis    |
199	| **Top-Bottom Split**   | Two related topics side by side    |
200	| **Timeline**           | Development history, roadmap       |
201	| **Dashboard Style**    | Multi-metric data dashboard        |
202	
203	---
204	
205	## VIII. Spacing Guidelines
206	
207	| Element              | Value    |
208	| -------------------- | -------- |
209	| Page margins         | 60px     |
210	| Title-to-content gap | 30-40px  |
211	| Module gap           | 60-80px  |
212	| Card gap             | 20-24px  |
213	| Card padding         | 20px     |
214	| Card border radius   | 16px     |
215	| Icon-to-text gap     | 15px     |
216	
217	---
218	
219	## IX. SVG Technical Constraints
220	
221	### Mandatory Rules
222	
223	1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
224	2. Use `<rect>` elements for backgrounds
225	3. Use `<tspan>` for text wrapping (no `<foreignObject>`)
226	4. Use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` for transparency
227	5. Define gradients using `<linearGradient>` within `<defs>`
228	
229	### Prohibited Elements
230	
231	The following SVG features are prohibited (not PPT-compatible):
232	
233	- `clipPath`, `mask`
234	- `<style>` tag, `class` attribute
235	- `foreignObject`
236	- `textPath`
237	- `animate*` animation elements
238	- `script`
239	- `marker`, `marker-end`
240	- `rgba()` color format (use HEX + opacity instead)
241	
242	### Shadow Implementation
243	
244	Since `filter` may affect PPT compatibility:
245	- Use subtle border color variations to simulate shadows
246	- Or accept that `filter` may be ignored in older PPT versions, though it works well in newer versions
247	
248	---
249	
250	## X. Placeholder Specification
251	
252	Templates use `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` format placeholders:
253	
254	| Placeholder            | Description              |
255	| ---------------------- | ------------------------ |
256	| `{{TITLE}}`            | Main title               |
257	| `{{SUBTITLE}}`         | Subtitle/department info |
258	| `{{SPEAKER_NAME}}`     | Speaker name             |
259	| `{{SPEAKER_TITLE}}`    | Speaker title/position   |
260	| `{{DATE}}`             | Date                     |
261	| `{{PAGE_TITLE}}`       | Page title               |
262	| `{{CHAPTER_NUM}}`      | Chapter number           |
263	| `{{CHAPTER_TITLE}}`    | Chapter title            |
264	| `{{CHAPTER_TITLE_EN}}` | Chapter English subtitle |
265	| `{{PAGE_NUM}}`         | Page number              |
266	| `{{CONTENT_AREA}}`     | Content area placeholder |
267	
268	---
269	
270	## XI. Color Application Examples
271	
272	### KPI Card Color Rules
273	
274	| Card Order | Border Color | Number Color | Applicable Content |
275	| ---------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------------------ |
276	| 1st        | `#4285F4`    | `#4285F4`    | Core projects/main metrics |
277	| 2nd        | `#34A853`    | `#34A853`    | Cost/efficiency metrics |
278	| 3rd        | `#EA4335`    | `#EA4335`    | Reliability/risk   |
279	| 4th        | `#FBBC04`    | `#FBBC04`    | Performance/growth |
280	
281	### List Item Colors
282	
283	- Use the four brand colors in rotation for list bullet colors
284	- Keep text in a consistent deep blue `#1A237E`
285	
286	---
287	
288	## XII. Usage Instructions
289	
290	1. Copy the template to the project directory `templates/`
291	2. Select the appropriate page type based on content needs
292	3. Use placeholders to mark content that needs replacement
293	4. Strictly follow the Google brand four-color scheme
294	5. Maintain generous whitespace to highlight key information
295	6. Data-driven: use large numbers + small labels to display KPIs
296	
297	---
298	
299	_This specification is based on Google Material Design principles, adapted for PPT Master project requirements_
300

# Design Specification & Content Outline
## Project: 1,001 Real-World Gen AI Use Cases from Google Cloud Customers

---

## I. Project Information

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Project Name** | gcloud_genai_usecases_ppt169_20260420 |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Slide Count** | 7 |
| **Style** | C) Top Consulting (conclusion-first, data-contextualized, SCQA-structured) |
| **Target Audience** | Enterprise technology leaders and digital transformation executives evaluating gen AI adoption |
| **Usage Occasion** | Executive briefing / strategic decision-making |
| **Core Message** | Gen AI has scaled from 101 to 1,001 real-world deployments in 18 months; structured by 11 industries × 6 agent types, with quantified ROI proving production readiness |
| **Template** | google_style |
| **Date** | April 2026 |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Format** | Standard 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Page Margins** | Left/Right 60px, Top 50px, Bottom 50px |
| **Safe Area** | x: 60–1220, y: 50–670 |
| **Title Area** | y=50, h=70px |
| **Content Area** | y=130, h=510px |
| **Footer** | y=670, h=50px |

---

## III. Visual Theme

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Style** | Top Consulting — clean, data-forward, conclusion-first |
| **Theme Mode** | Light (white background + Google brand color accents) |
| **Tone** | Professional, authoritative, strategic, data-grounded |

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| **Google Blue** | `#4285F4` | Primary titles, key data, KPI card borders (1st), chart series 1 |
| **Google Green** | `#34A853` | Positive indicators, growth metrics, KPI card borders (2nd) |
| **Google Red** | `#EA4335` | Emphasis, warnings, KPI card borders (3rd) |
| **Google Yellow** | `#FBBC04` | Accent, secondary emphasis, KPI card borders (4th) |
| **Deep Navy** | `#1A237E` | All primary text, page titles, headings |
| **Body Text** | `#5F6368` | Body content, descriptions |
| **Light Gray BG** | `#F8F9FA` | Card backgrounds, table alternating rows |
| **Border Gray** | `#E8EAED` | Dividers, table borders |
| **Page Background** | `#FFFFFF` | Main page background |

### Gradient (Top Bar)
- linearGradient: `#4285F4 → #EA4335 → #FBBC04 → #34A853`, h=6px, full width

### Title Underline (Four-Color Segments)
- Blue 150px → Red 70px → Yellow 70px → Green 170px; stroke-width 4px

---

## IV. Typography System

**Font Stack**: `system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`

| Level | Usage | Size | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Cover main title | 52px | 700 |
| H2 | Page main title | 36px | 700 |
| H3 | Section/module title | 24px | 600 |
| H4 | Card title / table header | 20px | 600 |
| P | Body content (dense baseline) | 18px | 400 |
| Data | Large KPI numbers | 52px | 700 |
| Label | Data labels / captions | 15px | 500 |
| Sub | Annotations / page numbers | 13px | 400 |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure
| Zone | Y Position | Height |
|---|---|---|
| Top four-color gradient bar | y=0 | h=6px |
| Title area | y=50 | h=70px |
| Content area | y=130 | h=510px |
| Footer (four-color dots + page num) | y=670 | h=50px |

### Layout Modes Used
- **Cover**: centered card on gradient background, left four-color vertical bar
- **Timeline / Arrow**: horizontal timeline with milestone callouts (Slide 2)
- **Matrix Grid**: industry × agent type heatmap (Slide 3)
- **Data Table**: structured use-case table with alternating rows (Slide 4)
- **KPI Cards**: 2×2 card grid with large numbers (Slide 5)
- **Three-Column Icons**: pattern clusters with icons (Slide 6)
- **Numbered List + Annotations**: takeaways with brief annotations (Slide 7)

### Spacing
| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Page margins | 60px |
| Title-to-content gap | 30px |
| Module gap | 40px |
| Card gap | 20px |
| Card padding | 20px |
| Card border radius | 12px |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Spec

**Source**: Built-in icon library (640+ icons)
**Placeholder syntax**: `{{icon:icon_name}}`

### Icon Inventory (Approved for use)

| Icon Name | Usage |
|---|---|
| `rocket` | Gen AI growth / acceleration |
| `arrow-trend-up` | 10× growth trajectory |
| `chart-line` | Data / analytics |
| `users` | Customer agents |
| `user` | Employee agents |
| `sparkles` | Creative agents |
| `code` | Code agents |
| `database` | Data agents |
| `shield` | Security agents |
| `car` | Automotive & Logistics |
| `factory` | Manufacturing |
| `hospital` | Healthcare |
| `dollar` | Financial Services |
| `shopping-cart` | Retail |
| `globe` | Telecommunications |
| `building` | Business & Professional Services |
| `trophy` | ROI / measurable outcomes |
| `lightbulb` | Strategic insights / takeaways |
| `circle-checkmark` | Production-ready / confirmed |
| `clock` | Time savings |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List

| Chart Type | Template Key | Used on Slide | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Timeline | `timeline` | Slide 2 | Visualize 10× growth from Apr 2024 to Oct 2025 |
| KPI Cards | `kpi_cards` | Slide 5 | Display 4 quantified ROI metrics |
| Custom matrix grid | (custom SVG) | Slide 3 | 11 industries × 6 agent types taxonomy |
| Custom table | (custom SVG) | Slide 4 | Automotive use cases by agent type |
| Three-column layout | (custom SVG) | Slide 6 | Cross-industry pattern clusters |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

No external images required. All visuals rendered via SVG shapes, charts, and icons.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Slide 1 — Cover (01_cover.svg style)
**Layout**: Centered card on light gradient background with left four-color vertical bar
**Title**: 1,001 Real-World Gen AI Use Cases from Google Cloud Customers
**Content**:
- Subtitle: "How 1,001 deployments across 11 industries and 6 agent types are defining the enterprise AI playbook"
- Source: Google Cloud | Updated October 2025
- Key stats row: "1,001 Use Cases · 11 Industries · 6 Agent Types · 10× Growth in 18 Months"
- Footer: "Source: Google Cloud Blog — Matt Renner & Matt A.V. Chaban"

---

### Slide 2 — Growth Trajectory (content page)
**Layout**: Horizontal timeline with two major milestones + growth arrow; supporting context text
**Title**: From 101 to 1,001: Gen AI Adoption Grew 10× in 18 Months
**Takeaway bar**: "Enterprise gen AI is in an early exponential phase — 400 new use cases added in the latest update alone"
**Content**:
- Timeline with two nodes:
  - **April 2024** (Cloud Next 24): 101 use cases — "First published; organizations across 11 industries"
  - **October 2025**: 1,001 use cases — "400 new entries in latest update; still 'only scratches the surface'"
- Large "10×" data callout in Google Blue (#4285F4)
- Duration label: "18 months"
- Supporting text: "Top companies, governments, researchers, and startups worldwide"
- Chart type: `timeline`

---

### Slide 3 — Taxonomy Matrix (content page)
**Layout**: Custom heatmap/matrix grid — 11 rows (industries) × 6 columns (agent types)
**Title**: 11 Industries × 6 Agent Types: A Taxonomy of Enterprise Gen AI
**Takeaway**: "Every major industry is now deploying agents across all six types — no vertical is untouched"
**Content**:
- Column headers (6 agent types): Customer · Employee · Creative · Code · Data · Security
- Row labels (11 industries):
  1. Automotive & Logistics
  2. Business & Professional Services
  3. Financial Services
  4. Healthcare & Life Sciences
  5. Hospitality & Travel
  6. Manufacturing, Industrial & Electronics
  7. Media, Marketing & Gaming
  8. Public Sector & Nonprofits
  9. Retail
  10. Technology
  11. Telecommunications
- Cell shading: filled cells in Google Blue (#4285F4 at 80% opacity) to indicate active deployment; all 66 cells filled (all industries × all agent types represented)
- Icon per column header: users (Customer), user (Employee), sparkles (Creative), code (Code), database (Data), shield (Security)
- Note below grid: "1,001 use cases organized across this framework — October 2025 edition"

---

### Slide 4 — Automotive & Logistics Deep Dive (content page)
**Layout**: Data table with alternating row shading; color-coded agent type column
**Title**: Automotive & Logistics: AI Agents From Cockpit to Curbside
**Takeaway**: "A single vertical demonstrates the full breadth: Customer to Code agents, factory floor to delivery route"
**Content**:
Table with columns: Agent Type | Organization | Use Case | Key Outcome

| Agent Type | Organization | Use Case | Key Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer | Mercedes-Benz | MBUX Virtual Assistant (Gemini/Vertex AI) for natural driver conversations | Natural language in-car navigation |
| Customer | LUXGEN (Taiwan EV) | AI agent on LINE via Vertex AI for customer questions | **30% workload reduction** |
| Customer | General Motors (OnStar) | Virtual assistant with conversational AI intent recognition | Improved intent recognition |
| Customer | Volkswagen of America | myVW app — query owner's manuals; multimodal dashboard indicator camera | Gemini multimodal capabilities |
| Customer | PODS / Tombras | "World's Smartest Billboard" adapting to NYC neighborhoods in real time | **6,000+ headlines, 299 neighborhoods, 29 hrs** |
| Employee | Toyota | AI platform for factory workers to build/deploy ML models | **10,000+ man-hours/year saved** |
| Employee | Uber | AI agents summarize CS communications; surface prior interaction context | Improved CS rep effectiveness |
| Employee | Rivian | Gemini in Google Workspace for research, learning, skill acquisition | Faster onboarding |
| Employee | Geotab | Workspace + Gemini across 4.7M connected vehicles; legal review, data filtering | Cross-functional productivity |
| Code | Renault Group (Ampere) | Enterprise Gemini Code Assist understanding company codebase & standards | Developer productivity for EV software |

- Agent Type cells color-coded: Customer = #4285F4, Employee = #34A853, Code = #EA4335
- Alternating row shading: #F8F9FA / #FFFFFF

---

### Slide 5 — Measurable ROI Highlights (content page)
**Layout**: 2×2 KPI card grid with large numbers, company labels, and brief context
**Title**: Quantified Impact: 500% ROI, 30% Workload Reduction, 10,000 Hours Saved
**Takeaway**: "These are production outcomes, not pilots — measurable ROI is being achieved at scale today"
**Content** — four KPI cards:

**Card 1 (Blue #4285F4)**:
- Number: 500%
- Label: Anticipated ROI
- Company: Mercari
- Context: Japan's largest online marketplace; AI-powered customer service also reducing employee workload 20%

**Card 2 (Green #34A853)**:
- Number: 30%
- Label: CS Workload Reduction
- Company: LUXGEN
- Context: Taiwan EV brand; Vertex AI chatbot handling customer queries

**Card 3 (Red #EA4335)**:
- Number: 10,000+
- Label: Man-Hours Saved / Year
- Company: Toyota
- Context: Factory AI platform enabling workers to build and deploy ML models

**Card 4 (Yellow #FBBC04)**:
- Number: 6,000+
- Label: Unique Ad Headlines
- Company: PODS / Tombras
- Context: "World's Smartest Billboard" generated across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just 29 hours

- Sub-note below cards: "Additional outcomes: Virgin Voyages — thousands of hyper-personalized ads via Veo; Figma — brand-approved assets in seconds"
- Chart type: `kpi_cards`

---

### Slide 6 — Cross-Industry Patterns (content page)
**Layout**: Three-column icon-header layout, each column with 2–3 company examples
**Title**: Common Patterns: Customer Assistants, Employee Productivity, and Creative Scale
**Takeaway**: "Three dominant deployment archetypes account for the majority of enterprise gen AI use cases today"
**Content**:

**Column 1 — Conversational Customer Agents** (icon: `users`, color: #4285F4)
- Most visible entry point across industries
- Mercedes-Benz: MBUX natural-language assistant
- GM OnStar: speaker intent recognition
- VW myVW: owner's manual queries + multimodal camera
- LUXGEN: 30% workload reduction via Vertex AI
- Commerzbank: gen AI-assisted customer service routing

**Column 2 — Employee Productivity Agents** (icon: `user`, color: #34A853)
- Broadest category across all 11 industries
- Uber: CS communication summarization + context surfacing
- Rivian: Gemini Workspace for research and onboarding
- Geotab: legal review, data filtering, research across 4.7M vehicles
- Routemark: release cycles shortened from weeks to days

**Column 3 — Creative & Scale Agents** (icon: `sparkles`, color: #EA4335)
- Fastest-growing frontier — text → multimodal
- Virgin Voyages: thousands of hyper-personalized video ads via Veo
- PODS / Tombras: 6,000+ real-time adaptive billboard headlines in 29 hours
- Figma: brand-approved image/asset generation in seconds

---

### Slide 7 — Strategic Takeaways (content page)
**Layout**: Numbered list with icon bullets, each item has a headline + 1-line annotation
**Title**: Takeaways: Where to Start and What to Expect from Enterprise Gen AI
**Takeaway**: "Early movers gain compounding advantages — the pace of enterprise gen AI adoption is accelerating"
**Content** — 5 takeaways:

1. **Gen AI is production-ready across all major industries** (icon: `circle-checkmark`, color: #4285F4)
   → 1,001 organizations from automotive to telecom are running gen AI in production, not pilots

2. **Customer and Employee agents are the most common entry points** (icon: `users`, color: #34A853)
   → Start here: highest ROI visibility, lowest organizational friction, fastest time to value

3. **Measurable ROI is achievable within months** (icon: `trophy`, color: #EA4335)
   → 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), 10,000+ hours saved (Toyota) — all in production

4. **Creative and Code agents are the fastest-growing frontier** (icon: `sparkles`, color: #FBBC04)
   → Multimodal creative production (Virgin Voyages, PODS) and enterprise code assistants (Renault Ampere) are scaling fast

5. **Adoption is accelerating — early movers compound their advantage** (icon: `rocket`, color: #4285F4)
   → 400 new use cases added in a single October 2025 update; 10× growth in 18 months shows no signs of plateauing

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **File naming** | Match SVG filenames: `01_cover.md`, `02_growth.md`, etc. |
| **Master doc** | `notes/total.md` with `#` heading lines per slide |
| **Presentation duration** | ~20 minutes (3 min/slide avg) |
| **Notes style** | Formal — professional talking points, data interpretation, conclusion-first |
| **Presentation purpose** | Inform + Persuade — equip enterprise leaders to act |

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

- viewBox: `0 0 1280 720` on every SVG
- No `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`, `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`, `rgba()`
- Use `<tspan>` for all text wrapping
- Use HEX + `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` for transparency
- Shadows: use border color variation or accept `filter` may be ignored in older PPT
- All text must be `<text>` elements, not embedded HTML
- No external font references — use system font stack only

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-Generation
- [x] Canvas 1280×720 confirmed
- [x] Google brand color palette defined
- [x] Typography system defined (P5 English-primary, 18px dense baseline)
- [x] Icon inventory verified against icons_index.json
- [x] All data points sourced from source_brief.md only
- [x] No fabricated statistics, company names, or outcomes

### Post-Generation
- [ ] All SVGs pass quality checker
- [ ] No prohibited SVG elements present
- [ ] Text does not overflow safe area (60–1220 x, 50–670 y)
- [ ] Four-color gradient bar present on all content pages
- [ ] KPI numbers readable at presentation size

---

## XIII. Next Steps

✅ Design spec complete. Template (google_style) ready. No AI image generation needed.
→ **Proceed directly to Executor phase** using `executor-base.md` + `executor-consultant-top.md`

### Slide 2 — Growth Trajectory (content page)
**Layout**: Horizontal timeline with two major milestones + growth arrow; supporting context text
**Title**: From 101 to 1,001: Gen AI Adoption Grew 10× in 18 Months
**Takeaway bar**: "Enterprise gen AI is in an early exponential phase — 400 new use cases added in the latest update alone"
**Content**:
- Timeline with two nodes:
  - **April 2024** (Cloud Next 24): 101 use cases — "First published; organizations across 11 industries"
  - **October 2025**: 1,001 use cases — "400 new entries in latest update; still 'only scratches the surface'"
- Large "10×" data callout in Google Blue (#4285F4)
- Duration label: "18 months"
- Supporting text: "Top companies, governments, researchers, and startups worldwide"
- Chart type: `timeline`

---

### Slide 3 — Taxonomy Matrix (content page)
**Layout**: Custom heatmap/matrix grid — 11 rows (industries) × 6 columns (agent types)
**Title**: 11 Industries × 6 Agent Types: A Taxonomy of Enterprise Gen AI
**Takeaway**: "Every major industry is now deploying agents across all six types — no vertical is untouched"
**Content**:
- Column headers (6 agent types): Customer · Employee · Creative · Code · Data · Security
- Row labels (11 industries):
  1. Automotive & Logistics
  2. Business & Professional Services
  3. Financial Services
  4. Healthcare & Life Sciences
  5. Hospitality & Travel
  6. Manufacturing, Industrial & Electronics
  7. Media, Marketing & Gaming
  8. Public Sector & Nonprofits
  9. Retail
  10. Technology
  11. Telecommunications
- Cell shading: filled cells in Google Blue (#4285F4 at 80% opacity) to indicate active deployment; all 66 cells filled (all industries × all agent types represented)
- Icon per column header: users (Customer), user (Employee), sparkles (Creative), code (Code), database (Data), shield (Security)
- Note below grid: "1,001 use cases organized across this framework — October 2025 edition"

---

### Slide 4 — Automotive & Logistics Deep Dive (content page)
**Layout**: Data table with alternating row shading; color-coded agent type column
**Title**: Automotive & Logistics: AI Agents From Cockpit to Curbside
**Takeaway**: "A single vertical demonstrates the full breadth: Customer to Code agents, factory floor to delivery route"
**Content**:
Table with columns: Agent Type | Organization | Use Case | Key Outcome

| Agent Type | Organization | Use Case | Key Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer | Mercedes-Benz | MBUX Virtual Assistant (Gemini/Vertex AI) for natural driver conversations | Natural language in-car navigation |
| Customer | LUXGEN (Taiwan EV) | AI agent on LINE via Vertex AI for customer questions | **30% workload reduction** |
| Customer | General Motors (OnStar) | Virtual assistant with conversational AI intent recognition | Improved intent recognition |
| Customer | Volkswagen of America | myVW app — query owner's manuals; multimodal dashboard indicator camera | Gemini multimodal capabilities |
| Customer | PODS / Tombras | "World's Smartest Billboard" adapting to NYC neighborhoods in real time | **6,000+ headlines, 299 neighborhoods, 29 hrs** |
| Employee | Toyota | AI platform for factory workers to build/deploy ML models | **10,000+ man-hours/year saved** |
| Employee | Uber | AI agents summarize CS communications; surface prior interaction context | Improved CS rep effectiveness |
| Employee | Rivian | Gemini in Google Workspace for research, learning, skill acquisition | Faster onboarding |
| Employee | Geotab | Workspace + Gemini across 4.7M connected vehicles; legal review, data filtering | Cross-functional productivity |
| Code | Renault Group (Ampere) | Enterprise Gemini Code Assist understanding company codebase & standards | Developer productivity for EV software |

- Agent Type cells color-coded: Customer = #4285F4, Employee = #34A853, Code = #EA4335
- Alternating row shading: #F8F9FA / #FFFFFF

---

### Slide 5 — Measurable ROI Highlights (content page)
**Layout**: 2×2 KPI card grid with large numbers, company labels, and brief context
**Title**: Quantified Impact: 500% ROI, 30% Workload Reduction, 10,000 Hours Saved
**Takeaway**: "These are production outcomes, not pilots — measurable ROI is being achieved at scale today"
**Content** — four KPI cards:

**Card 1 (Blue #4285F4)**:
- Number: 500%
- Label: Anticipated ROI
- Company: Mercari
- Context: Japan's largest online marketplace; AI-powered customer service also reducing employee workload 20%

**Card 2 (Green #34A853)**:
- Number: 30%
- Label: CS Workload Reduction
- Company: LUXGEN
- Context: Taiwan EV brand; Vertex AI chatbot handling customer queries

**Card 3 (Red #EA4335)**:
- Number: 10,000+
- Label: Man-Hours Saved / Year
- Company: Toyota
- Context: Factory AI platform enabling workers to build and deploy ML models

**Card 4 (Yellow #FBBC04)**:
- Number: 6,000+
- Label: Unique Ad Headlines
- Company: PODS / Tombras
- Context: "World's Smartest Billboard" generated across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just 29 hours

- Sub-note below cards: "Additional outcomes: Virgin Voyages — thousands of hyper-personalized ads via Veo; Figma — brand-approved assets in seconds"
- Chart type: `kpi_cards`

---

### Slide 6 — Cross-Industry Patterns (content page)
**Layout**: Three-column icon-header layout, each column with 2–3 company examples
**Title**: Common Patterns: Customer Assistants, Employee Productivity, and Creative Scale
**Takeaway**: "Three dominant deployment archetypes account for the majority of enterprise gen AI use cases today"
**Content**:

**Column 1 — Conversational Customer Agents** (icon: `users`, color: #4285F4)
- Most visible entry point across industries
- Mercedes-Benz: MBUX natural-language assistant
- GM OnStar: speaker intent recognition
- VW myVW: owner's manual queries + multimodal camera
- LUXGEN: 30% workload reduction via Vertex AI
- Commerzbank: gen AI-assisted customer service routing

**Column 2 — Employee Productivity Agents** (icon: `user`, color: #34A853)
- Broadest category across all 11 industries
- Uber: CS communication summarization + context surfacing
- Rivian: Gemini Workspace for research and onboarding
- Geotab: legal review, data filtering, research across 4.7M vehicles
- Routemark: release cycles shortened from weeks to days

**Column 3 — Creative & Scale Agents** (icon: `sparkles`, color: #EA4335)
- Fastest-growing frontier — text → multimodal
- Virgin Voyages: thousands of hyper-personalized video ads via Veo
- PODS / Tombras: 6,000+ real-time adaptive billboard headlines in 29 hours
- Figma: brand-approved image/asset generation in seconds

---

### Slide 7 — Strategic Takeaways (content page)
**Layout**: Numbered list with icon bullets, each item has a headline + 1-line annotation
**Title**: Takeaways: Where to Start and What to Expect from Enterprise Gen AI
**Takeaway**: "Early movers gain compounding advantages — the pace of enterprise gen AI adoption is accelerating"
**Content** — 5 takeaways:

1. **Gen AI is production-ready across all major industries** (icon: `circle-checkmark`, color: #4285F4)
   → 1,001 organizations from automotive to telecom are running gen AI in production, not pilots

2. **Customer and Employee agents are the most common entry points** (icon: `users`, color: #34A853)
   → Start here: highest ROI visibility, lowest organizational friction, fastest time to value

3. **Measurable ROI is achievable within months** (icon: `trophy`, color: #EA4335)
   → 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), 10,000+ hours saved (Toyota) — all in production

4. **Creative and Code agents are the fastest-growing frontier** (icon: `sparkles`, color: #FBBC04)
   → Multimodal creative production (Virgin Voyages, PODS) and enterprise code assistants (Renault Ampere) are scaling fast

5. **Adoption is accelerating — early movers compound their advantage** (icon: `rocket`, color: #4285F4)
   → 400 new use cases added in a single October 2025 update; 10× growth in 18 months shows no signs of plateauing

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **File naming** | Match SVG filenames: `01_cover.md`, `02_growth.md`, etc. |
| **Master doc** | `notes/total.md` with `#` heading lines per slide |
| **Presentation duration** | ~20 minutes (3 min/slide avg) |
| **Notes style** | Formal — professional talking points, data interpretation, conclusion-first |
| **Presentation purpose** | Inform + Persuade — equip enterprise leaders to act |

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

- viewBox: `0 0 1280 720` on every SVG
- No `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`, `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`, `rgba()`
- Use `<tspan>` for all text wrapping
- Use HEX + `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` for transparency
- Shadows: use border color variation or accept `filter` may be ignored in older PPT
- All text must be `<text>` elements, not embedded HTML
- No external font references — use system font stack only

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-Generation
- [x] Canvas 1280×720 confirmed
- [x] Google brand color palette defined
- [x] Typography system defined (P5 English-primary, 18px dense baseline)
- [x] Icon inventory verified against icons_index.json
- [x] All data points sourced from source_brief.md only
- [x] No fabricated statistics, company names, or outcomes

### Post-Generation
- [ ] All SVGs pass quality checker
- [ ] No prohibited SVG elements present
- [ ] Text does not overflow safe area (60–1220 x, 50–670 y)
- [ ] Four-color gradient bar present on all content pages
- [ ] KPI numbers readable at presentation size

---

## XIII. Next Steps

✅ Design spec complete. Template (google_style) ready. No AI image generation needed.
→ **Proceed directly to Executor phase** using `executor-base.md` + `executor-consultant-top.md`

1	# Executor Common Guidelines
2	
3	> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Template Adherence Rules
8	
9	If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:
10	
11	| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
12	|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
13	| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
14	| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
15	| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
16	| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
17	| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |
18	
19	### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)
20	
21	Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:
22	
23	```
24	📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
25	🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
26	```
27	
28	- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
29	- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)
34	
35	> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.
36	
37	Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.
38	
39	**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Execution Guidelines
44	
45	- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
46	- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
47	- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
48	- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
49	  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
50	  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52	
53	### SVG File Naming Convention
54	
55	File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`
56	
57	- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67	
68	**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:
69	
70	```xml
71	<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`
77	
78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87	
88	**Adaptation rules**:
89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109	
110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):
168	
169	```bash
170	# 1. Split speaker notes
171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```
180

# Executor Common Guidelines

> Style-specific content is in the corresponding `executor-{style}.md`. Technical constraints are in shared-standards.md.

---

## 1. Template Adherence Rules

If template files exist in the project's `templates/` directory, the template structure must be followed:

| Page Type | Corresponding Template | Adherence Rules |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Cover | `01_cover.svg` | Inherit background, decorative elements, layout structure; replace placeholder content |
| Chapter | `02_chapter.svg` | Inherit numbering style, title position, decorative elements |
| Content | `03_content.svg` | Inherit header/footer styles; **content area may be freely laid out** |
| Ending | `04_ending.svg` | Inherit background, thank-you message position, contact info layout |
| TOC | `02_toc.svg` | **Optional**: Inherit TOC title, list styles |

### Page-Template Mapping Declaration (Required Output)

Before generating each page, you must explicitly output which template (or "free design") is used:

```
📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
```

- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)

> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.

Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.

**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.

---

## 3. Execution Guidelines

- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules

### SVG File Naming Convention

File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`

- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline

---

## 4. Icon Usage

Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)

**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:

```xml
<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
```

> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.

**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`

> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.

Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`

---

## 5. Chart Reference

When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.

**Adaptation rules**:
- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline

> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`

---

## 6. Image Handling

Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":

| Status | Source | Handling |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |

**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`

**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text

---

## 7. Font Usage

Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:

| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
|------|--------------------|--------------------|
| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |

---

## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework

### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document

After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.

**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.

**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.

**Requirements**:

- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory

### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files

Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.

**File naming convention**:

- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)

---

## 9. Next Steps After Completion

> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.

**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

39	**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Execution Guidelines
44	
45	- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
46	- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
47	- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
48	- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
49	  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
50	  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52	
53	### SVG File Naming Convention
54	
55	File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`
56	
57	- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67	
68	**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:
69	
70	```xml
71	<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`
77	
78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87	
88	**Adaptation rules**:
89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109	
110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):
168	
169	```bash

171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
173	
174	### Notes Example
175	
176	```markdown
177	# 03_strategic_path
178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
182	
183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
185	
186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
188	
189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
190	
191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
192	Duration: 3 minutes
193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
199	
200	### Content Level
201	
202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
206	
207	### Visual Level
208	
209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
213	
214	### Notes Level
215	
216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration
219
